title: Information gain
content: In content planning, information gain is the useful new information a page adds beyond what the reader can already find elsewhere.

meta.why: A new example, documented test, or original explanation is what makes a reader pick this page over the other pages that cover the same topic.
meta.example: A guide includes a documented comparison from the author’s own evaluation, with the method and limitations visible.
meta.check: What will this page offer that a reader cannot find elsewhere? Name that contribution in the brief, and confirm the writer has the records or experience to support it.
meta.limitation: Information gain in this editorial sense has no public Google score, and novelty alone does not make information accurate or useful.
meta.sources: Google Search Central: helpful, reliable content | https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content | Platform documentation
